had many whales near the ship during the day, but the albatrosses had left us.
war corvette de mercij, from portsmouth, sailing from rio de janeiro to valparaiso.

shook out the anchor rope, they hauled it down.?? | changed meridian by the w: 40,75 miles.

saw an english man-of-war near us in the flood. she was greeted by captain huijghens with 9 guns. (the englishman) thanked with 7 guns. | sailed under small sail to wait for the sternmost ship. made the fore topsail fast. | changed meridian by the west: 13,25 miles.

first watch: furled the fore topsail, took the last reef in the main topsail | changed meridian 2 miles

at daybreak they could see none of their ships. saw three ships to windward, but could not tell whether those ships belonged to the convoy. | morning watch: took in the topgallant yards. middle watch: courses breeze with storm squalls, later less wind. | changed meridian by the e 11,5 miles

saw 4 ships to windward and one close by to leeward ahead. first watch: they make the signal of reconnaissance to the ship to leeward. the ship answered this with a counter signal. they shortened sail to stay by her. | at daybreak they set the jib and the main topsail | changed meridian by the e 5,25 miles
sometimes fired a fog gun. | saw the ship that belonged to our convoy close to us. | morning watch: mist and rain, thick hazy sky. changed meridian 2.5 miles to the east. | variable
changed meridian by the w 6,5 miles

saw 5 ships to leeward, they make the signal of reconnaissance: strike the fore topsail and 2 sheets. they could not see whether (those other ships) gave the counter signal. | changed meridian by the w 7,5 miles | fine
changed meridian by the w 0,75 miles
saw our merchantman | at daybreak: took the 4th reef in the fore topsail | changed meridian by the w 1,25 miles
changed meridian by the e 2,75 miles
furled the cross-jack and after tacking about the nw they furled the fore topsail. | changed meridian by the e 2 miles

saw that their merchantman had got clear of them. then sailed with little sail. | saw that the 2nd main shroud of the larboard side was broken, above the swifter. | changed meridian by the w 8,75 miles
afternoon: the main topsail torn, mended it. | changed meridian by the w 11,25
saw a ship in the se, which was lying near us. | set the fore topsail and the studding sails, bent the main topsail again. | changed meridian by the e 2,25 miles
forenoon: hoisted the topgallant yards. | changed meridian by the e 7,75 miles | fine
changed meridian by the east 7,25 | fine

saw a ship in the ese. | changed meridian by the w 12 miles.

forenoon: saw porto santo in the nw by n, (estimated) 8.5 miles. changed meridian to the west 26.5 miles. morning+evening: bore porto santo nw by n (estimated) 4.5 miles
see 2 ships. (after some tacking) they prove to be captain huijghens and a merchantman.
1 of the merchantmen thanked for the convoy with 5 shots. captain huijghens thanked with 3 shots.

the commander of the soldiers was put in irons. he is accused of indecent things: he is said to have played with the manhood of a boy (and wanted the same from that boy). | they make the signal to speak to the commander.

council of war on board with captain huijghens (with the captain, 2 commanders, the commander of the soldiers and the previously named boy). towards noon the prisoner came back on board. | afternoon watch + first watch: waiting for the merchantmen. | fine

forenoon watch: i (the clerk) read the sentence on the commander of the soldiers. (all the ship's company listened). the latter was to be put ashore at the first opportunity, his pay was to be confiscated, he would never again be allowed to serve the country. | fine
main topsail reef-rope (?) in pieces, brought another aloft. | fine
captain huijghens made the signal to speak to our captain. | fine
aw: saw a ship in the n
saw a ship in the wnw | at 7 o'clock they tack to the sse. forenoon: tack to the w
captain huijghens takes leave with exchange of flag and pennant and 9 salute shots. | with damp
a sailor, anthonie meijer, in irons for stealing a buffalo...?
fore topmast in the hounds broken to pieces. lowered it and made a new fid hole in it.

seaman anthonij meijer, out of the irons again and beaten with ropes' ends by 2 quartermasters; then the articles of war were read to him by the clerk and afterwards the captain gave him a reprimand before the whole ship's company. | fine

aw: bark from the north with a french pennant, which fired 2 shots so that the topsails would be backed, but she sailed on. whereupon the bark stood to the south. | flag and pennant for french bark | fine
see a bark with 3 other ships | fine
afternoon: at anchor with 1/2 of the day's cable

fetched 4 passengers from the english bark on board. some gentlemen of the government on board from shore. at departure 9 shots. captain goes ashore. welcomed by the fort with 13 shots. | a dutch bark bound for martinique saluted with 11 shots. thanked with 9. | the french privateer departed. we fired 4 times with live shot at him (…). but he continued his course.
a dutch frigate came in, saluted with 7 shots. we with 5.. a large fleet of ships that passed to the n. | hoisted the jib rigging.

16 merchant skippers on board to pass the time. christiaan van derp, the commander of the soldiers, put on a bark to martinique. | boat and prau came in. each saluted with 7 shots, we with 5. several barques sailed out and came in. dutch merchantman came in, which came from lisbon. had been 26 days on the way. | struck the main yard and topmast. hoisted the passjaar (?) flag to passjaar. spliced the 2 foremost shrouds of the main rigging. | fine
dutch frigate came in, which had sailed on 5 sept.. fetching water with a boat from a merchantman. | fine
bark that went to sea saluted with 9 shots. thanked with 7. | fetched 2 boats with fresh water on board. | patched the standing rigging with salve. set the dutch pumps to work.
seaman christoffel colmer died | a bark sailed to sea. | fine
several gentlemen of the government of the shore on board. at departure 9 shots.

fetched a boat with fresh water. sent 23 whole and 12 half pigs. | 2 barks from martinique (1 saluted with 8 and the other with 9 shots, we thanked with 5 and 7 shots respectively) and 1 from granada passed. | received 6 carpenters from the merchantmen on board and went to caulk the ship outside. rose the masts.
sent 7 whole and 5 half pigs ashore | a snow-ship came in.. schooner from new england came in: they 9, we 7 shots. | tarred the yards.
fetched 29 whole and 11 half hogsheads of water | squally with moisture

english man-of-war passed. | fetched 14 hogsheads of water | squally
soldier put in irons. a seaman, louis rikkelman, died. | tarred the ship's outside
dutch merchantman from cork came in with meat and butter. skipper benedictus rip | fine

clerk was sent to the ship of skipper roelof zuiderstroom to fetch a seaman who had abused his skipper with brutal words. at the tops he was put in irons. a statement against him was also | fetched 7 whole and 7 half hogsheads of water | squally
seaman of skipper david de jong put in irons. | barque from martinique came in. she saluted with 9 shots and so did we. | rove new top and fore braces.

court martial on the seaman of skipper roelof zuijderstroom | fetched 7 whole and 5 half hogsheads of water. | 3 shots with live shot at an english bark which showed no flags. (she came towards us) and we hailed her.

9 half hogsheads of water brought aboard. | 2 shots with live shot at 2 barks to get astern of them.

english bark. | 3 shots with live shot at an english bark which showed no flag. | fine

saw only 3 of the merchantmen. | furled the fore topsail and let her drift so. took the last reef in the main topsail. first watch: sailed with the main topsail and storm foresail to stay with the merchantman. | lightning | hollow sea

took the 3rd reef in the main topsail. vw: main topsail yard in pieces | squally weather

took the 3rd reef in the topsail (to wait for the merchantmen). gave the signal to the merchantmen to make more sail.
seaman francisi de roze died | hove to to the nne (to wait for the merchantmen). (2 hours later) they braced off again. first watch: main topsail splits. | squally
foremost head rope of the mizzen shrouds broken | fine
aw: tacking about the n | fine
seaman thomas braun died | main topmast swifters shoring (?) | fine

chief gunner harmanus van seldam, died | had again to wait for skipper mobek
waited for the merchantmen. filled 22 hogsheads with salt water. afternoon watch-first watch: let the topsail shiver, to stay with the merchantmen. | fine

waited for the merchantmen. could not see captain evertse. could not see captain mobek from aloft. then braced about.
braced off at 8 o'clock. | could not see skipper cornelis everts, waited for him. | squally

the main topmast cracked (snapped?) just above the trestletrees on the starboard side. forenoon: took a reef in the cracked topmast. captain the pis end of the tuitouw and the tuitouw as well as the plechttouw and the anchors..
shook all the reefs out of the topsail. captain veered 17 fathoms out of the hawser and "let the same ride on 1/2 cable's bitt?"
main topsail yard on the port side breaks. repair work.
ordered the main topsail aloft. | sounded the depth.

see 5 ships in the ssw. | changed meridian by the east 5,5 miles. | good

changed meridian by the e 6,25 miles | first watch: hollow sea
pumped 16 inches. secured the fore topsail because of a leak in the bow. pumped a few hours. forenoon watch: leak stopped. | changed meridian by the w 12 miles.
set the fore topsail and crossjack. | changed meridian by the w 6,75 miles.
saw a ship steering ese. | take a reef out of the main topsail. | changed meridian by the w 6,75 miles. | fine

at 16.00h took bearing of goudstaart north, 2.5 miles. on 6 september entered the roads of texel. the ship continues to sail back and forth between texel and flushing. the journal ends on 5 november at amsterdam.
